content: Pheniramine, also known by its International Nonproprietary Name (INN) and trade name Avil, is an antihistamine with anticholinergic properties. It is primarily used to treat allergic conditions such as hay fever and urticaria. This medication is known to have relatively strong sedative effects and is sometimes used off-label as an over-the-counter sleep aid, similar to other sedating antihistamines like diphenhydramine. Pheniramine is also commonly included in eye drops formulated for the treatment of allergic conjunctivitis. It is generally sold in combination with other medications rather than as a standalone drug, although some formulations containing only pheniramine are available. For instance, the product Neo Citran contains pheniramine as one of its components. Derivatives of pheniramine include chlorpheniramine, dexchlorpheniramine, dexbropheniramine, deschlorpheniramine, triprolidine, and brompheniramine. Additionally, two halogenated derivatives, iodopheniramine and fluorpheniramine, are currently being studied for their potential use in combination therapies for malaria and certain cancers. The halogenation of pheniramine significantly increases its potency, enhancing it by approximately 20-fold. Pheniramine may cause side effects such as drowsiness and bradycardia. Overdosage can result in sleep disturbances and, in severe cases, seizures, particularly when combined with alcohol. Long-term use of pheniramine in combination with cortisol should be avoided, as it may lead to reduced levels of adrenaline (epinephrine), which could result in loss of consciousness.
